content.text: I reviewed the brief line by line against the release (income statement, cash flow, segment tables, and the OpenAI/constant-currency reconciliations).

facts.evidence: Revenue for the quarter ended June 30, 2026, was $90.0 billion, an 18% increase year-over-year (17% in constant currency).
GAAP diluted earnings per share (EPS) was $4.81, up 32%

non-GAAP diluted EPS was $4.74, up 23%. ... non-GAAP net income, which excludes the impact from investments in OpenAI ... The release notes that non-GAAP results exclude the impact from investments in OpenAI
Intelligent Cloud revenue was $39.3 billion, up 32% (31% in constant currency), driven by a 43% increase in Azure and other cloud services revenue.
Operating income was $40.6 billion, up 18% year-over-year.
Microsoft Cloud revenue was $59.3 billion, up 27%
commercial remaining performance obligation increased 84% to $678 billion

Net cash from operations was $55.4 billion for the quarter, while additions to property and equipment were $35.8 billion. (Quarterly figure correct at $35,802 million; the brief omits the $17,079 million prior-year quarter comparison but states nothing wrong.)

The release notes that discrete items, including a $3.2 billion gain from an investment in Anthropic, resulted in a $0.27 benefit to diluted EPS compared to forward-looking guidance provided on April 29, 2026.
More Personal Computing revenue was $12.9 billion, down 4% (5% in constant currency) (the brief does not characterize it as the only declining segment, but the figures, period and basis are right)

claims.claim: Revenue for the quarter ended June 30, 2026 was $90.0 billion.
Revenue increased 18% year over year.
Revenue increased 17% in constant currency.
Operating income was $40.6 billion, up 18% year over year.
GAAP net income was $35.8 billion, up 31%.
Non-GAAP net income, which excludes the impact from investments in OpenAI, was $35.3 billion, up 22%.
GAAP diluted EPS was $4.81, up 32%.
Non-GAAP diluted EPS was $4.74, up 23%.
Discrete items, including a $3.2 billion gain from an investment in Anthropic, resulted in a $0.27 benefit to diluted EPS compared with the forward-looking guidance provided on April 29, 2026.
Intelligent Cloud revenue was $39.3 billion, up 32% (31% in constant currency).
Intelligent Cloud growth was driven by a 43% increase in Azure and other cloud services revenue.
Productivity and Business Processes revenue was $37.8 billion, up 14%.
Microsoft 365 Commercial cloud revenue increased 14% on a reported basis.
More Personal Computing revenue was $12.9 billion, down 4% (down 5% in constant currency).
Windows OEM and Devices revenue decreased 7%.
XBOX content and services revenue decreased 10%.
Microsoft Cloud revenue was $59.3 billion, up 27%.
Commercial remaining performance obligation increased 84% to $678 billion.
Microsoft will provide forward-looking guidance on its earnings conference call and webcast in connection with this quarterly earnings announcement.
No specific numerical guidance figures are provided in the text of the release itself.
Microsoft returned $10.2 billion to shareholders in dividends and share repurchases in the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2026.
Total cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments were $76.8 billion as of June 30, 2026.
Net cash from operations was $55.4 billion for the quarter.
Additions to property and equipment were $35.8 billion for the quarter.
The release highlights a $3.2 billion gain from an investment in Anthropic and lower-than-expected Voluntary Retirement Program expenses as discrete items impacting results.
More Personal Computing revenue decreased 4%, with declines in Windows OEM and Devices (-7%) and XBOX content and services (-10%).
The release notes that non-GAAP results exclude the impact from investments in OpenAI.
The impact from investments in OpenAI resulted in a $480 million increase to net income in the quarter.
